$comment: Dependency licence policy for ADR 0017. allowedLicenses is the allowlist; exceptions are manual, reasoned overrides for a package whose nuspec cannot be read as an SPDX expression (a bundled licence file, an old-style licenseUrl-only nuspec) or whose licence is genuinely off the allowlist but permitted under ADR 0017 (LGPL-3.0 as a separate CI process, an EULA that never leaves samples/). An exception matches by package id; every exception must carry a non-empty reason or the run fails before any package is evaluated.

exceptions.reason: ADR 0017 standing exception: invoked as a separate CI process, never linked or shipped. Its nuspec declares <license type="file">licenses/LICENSE.txt</license>, which is the GNU Lesser General Public License v3 text; no SPDX expression is present to read automatically.

ADR 0017 standing exception: referenced only by samples/webapi-basic (legacy), isolated from the root build by samples/Directory.Build.props, and never vendored into a release artifact. Its nuspec declares <license type="file">NET_Library_EULA_ENU.txt</license>, the Microsoft .NET Library EULA (requireLicenseAcceptance=true), the only non-OSI licence in the repository.

Samples-only (samples/webapi-basic, modern side). Its nuspec predates SPDX <license> expressions and exposes only a licenseUrl pointing at aspnet/AspNetCore's Apache-2.0 LICENSE.txt; confirmed Apache-2.0 in ADR 0002.

Build-and-test-only local tool (mutation testing), never shipped. Its nuspec declares <license type="file">LICENSE</license>, the Apache License 2.0 text; no SPDX expression is present to read automatically. Confirmed Apache-2.0 in ADR 0002.

Build-and-test-only transitive dependency of Verify.XunitV3 (snapshot testing). Its nuspec declares <license type="file">OsmfEula.txt</license>, which is not the code licence itself but VerifyTests' Open Source Maintenance Fee rider on top of the underlying MIT-licensed project (the rider text says so directly: "an open source software project licensed under the MIT"). The MIT code licence and the maintenance-fee rider are already tracked for Verify.XunitV3 in ADR 0002 and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md via the SmallRevenue exemption in Directory.Build.props; this entry extends that same treatment to the base Verify package the fee rider actually documents.

ADR 0017 standing exception (third): transitive dependency of Sarif.Sdk (Core, Cli), pulled in via Microsoft.Diagnostics.Tracing.TraceEvent's dependency group for .NETStandard2.0, exclude="Build,Analyzers". Its nuspec has no <license> element, only a licenseUrl fwlink; resolved by hand (M0-010) to https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/perfview_library_license.htm, "MICROSOFT SOFTWARE LICENSE TERMS - MICROSOFT PERFVIEW .NET LIBRARY" - a restrictive Microsoft EULA, not the MIT licence its sibling TraceEvent carries (PerfView's GitHub source is MIT; this specific old NuGet package binary predates that and was never re-licensed on nuget.org). Verified it is never actually shipped: the package is an old-style nuspec with no lib/ folder, so SDK-style PackageReference restore does not copy eventRegister.exe or Microsoft.Diagnostics.Tracing.EventSource.dll into build output (checked src/Equiv.Core/bin and src/Equiv.Cli/bin directly - neither file is present). It is restored (present in the lock file and the NuGet cache) to satisfy the dependency graph but never linked into a release artifact, the same standing as the other two exceptions above.
